response.goal: Use No-Shell Agent Architect MCP to operate its own free public beta: collect GitHub and MCP Registry signals, stage one safe public feedback post, triage feedback into product fixes, and design a Gmail/community permissioned connector v1 without using secrets, cookies, paid APIs, or live posting.
response.one_line_strategy: Turn a vague automation request into a tool stack, permissioned account route, copy-paste agent command, dry-run path, QA/audit scorecard, and live-action boundary.

recommended_stack.label: Human boundary checkpoint
recommended_stack.why: Real money, public publishing, account changes, and credential exposure need a visible live-action boundary.
recommended_stack.setup: Write exactly what the agent can automate through permissioned connectors, what stays draft/staged, and what requires an exact live-action instruction.
recommended_stack.caution: A boundary is not the finish line; fix upstream causes and automate everything safely up to that boundary.

recommended_stack.label: Chrome plugin
recommended_stack.why: Use the user’s logged-in browser state only when a task genuinely depends on cookies or account UI.
recommended_stack.setup: Prefer APIs first; use Chrome only for logged-in site state.
recommended_stack.caution: Use it inside a declared scope. Never inspect passwords, cookies, recovery codes, or unrelated account areas.

recommended_stack.label: Permissioned account automation pattern
recommended_stack.why: Lets agents read, draft, stage, submit, or post through approved account sessions while preserving scope, allowlists, dry-run mode, and an action ledger.
recommended_stack.setup: Define connector or session source, OAuth/browser permission, allowed read filters, allowed destinations, draft-vs-live actions, rollback path, and audit log location.
recommended_stack.caution: This is not 2FA, cookie, or mailbox bypass; it only runs inside the user-granted scope.

recommended_stack.label: Browser plugin
recommended_stack.why: Use it to open localhost, click through the UI, and catch layout/runtime breakage before calling work finished.
recommended_stack.setup: Use the installed Browser plugin when a local web target or screenshot QA is needed.
recommended_stack.caution: Do not use it as a replacement for API tests or source-code review.

recommended_stack.label: Dynamic workflow orchestrator skill
recommended_stack.why: Splits large work into phases, bounded side tasks, integration, validation, and Obsidian trace.
recommended_stack.setup: Use when the work spans multiple modules, notes, or agents.
recommended_stack.caution: Keep the main agent responsible for final judgment and integration.

recommended_stack.label: GitHub plugin
recommended_stack.why: Handles repo, PR, issue, CI, and code review work without manual browser wandering.
recommended_stack.setup: Use for repository inspection, PR feedback, or CI failures.
recommended_stack.caution: Repository creation may still need account/session support if CLI access is missing.

execution_phases.name: 1. Intake
execution_phases.action: Restate the real outcome, inputs, target user, available accounts, and forbidden actions.

execution_phases.name: 2. Stack route
execution_phases.action: Choose the smallest tool stack that can actually complete the workflow, not just produce files.

execution_phases.name: 3. Permission route
execution_phases.action: Define the OAuth/plugin/session source, read filters, destination allowlist, draft-vs-live split, and action ledger before touching account data.

execution_phases.name: 4. Dry run
execution_phases.action: Run the workflow on a safe sample input and capture the evidence.

execution_phases.name: 5. QA/audit
execution_phases.action: Check output correctness, missing source data, human boundary, and recovery path.

execution_phases.name: 6. Handoff
execution_phases.action: Return a copy-paste command, result scorecard, and next-run checklist.

account_automation.safe_default: Start in read-only and draft/staging mode, then promote one exact live action.
account_automation.connector_route: Use an official API, MCP/plugin, or logged-in browser session only for the named community/account and destination.
automatable_actions: Read or search only the allowed label, query, thread, page, or destination.
Classify, summarize, extract tasks, prepare replies/posts/forms, and save drafts or staged outputs.
Record a compact action ledger with timestamps, target IDs, validation result, and remaining live action.
required_controls: Read filters and destination allowlist are explicit.
Draft/staging actions are separated from live send/post/submit actions.
Logs redact private content and never store tokens, cookies, or recovery codes.
account_automation.draft_vs_live: Publish, schedule, delete, or edit public posts only when the user requested that exact destination/action after rules are checked; otherwise create staged drafts.
account_automation.rollback: Keep the draft/staged artifact ID and the last safe checkpoint so a failed run can be retried, edited, or discarded without guessing.
forbidden_bypass: No raw cookie, token, password, recovery-code, or unrestricted mailbox harvesting.
No public, financial, identity, billing, or irreversible action outside the declared live-action scope.

permissioned_connector_v1.goal: Use No-Shell Agent Architect MCP to operate its own free public beta: collect GitHub and MCP Registry signals, stage one safe public feedback post, triage feedback into product fixes, and design a Gmail/community permissioned connector v1 without using secrets, cookies, paid APIs, or live posting.
forbidden_bypass: No password, cookie, recovery-code, or 2FA bypass.
No unrestricted inbox, account, browser, or community scraping.
No live send, publish, delete, billing, identity, or irreversible action without an exact live-action instruction.
validation: Run on one safe sample scope first.
Produce a draft, staged post, preview, or review queue item before any live action.
Record an action ledger entry with no raw private content or token values.
Report PASS/WARN/FAIL with the remaining exact live action.
recovery: If auth is missing, stop at connector setup instructions and keep the drafted artifact.
If destination rules are missing, stage the draft and mark rule_check_required.
If validation fails, fix the prompt/tool route before trying a broader account scope.

required_scope_contract.connector_source: Official API, approved platform connector, or logged-in browser session owned by the user.
required_scope_contract.live_boundary: Publish, comment, edit, delete, or schedule only after the exact platform, destination, and final copy are approved.

v1_run_card: Read or open the destination rules before staging copy.
Create one feedback-seeking post draft with no hype or fake traction claims.
Stage the draft and record not_posted unless the live action is explicitly approved.
Run the public beta signal collector after posting or after the scheduled observation window.

human_boundaries: Do not expose API keys, cookies, or private customer data.
Do not bypass login, 2FA, OAuth consent, or account permissions.
Do not present a blocked gate as completion; repair the upstream cause first.
Keep a short audit trace: input, tools used, validation, remaining manual step.
Public publish or schedule actions may run only through an approved connector/session, an allowlisted destination, and an exact live-action instruction; draft and staging can be automated first.
Split the workflow into dry-run, review, and live phases.

dry_run_tests: Run the workflow on one safe sample input.
Confirm every produced artifact maps back to the original goal.
Check that no private secret, account token, or irreversible live action is required for the dry run.
Use a permissioned connector/session on one allowed sample: label, query, thread, URL, or destination.
Create only a draft, staged post, preview, or review item unless the exact live action was requested.
Write an action ledger entry without storing raw private content, tokens, cookies, or recovery codes.
qa_checks: Does the result complete the actual workflow, not only create a file or UI?
Are source-backed facts separated from estimates or assumptions?
Can a non-developer follow the first command without decoding jargon?
Is there a recovery path for missing input, provider failure, or auth failure?
Are OAuth scopes, session source, read filters, and destination allowlists explicit?
Is draft/staging clearly separated from live send, publish, submit, delete, billing, or account changes?
If community posting is involved, were the destination rules checked before any live action?
audit_checks: Tool stack is minimal and justified.
Permissioned account automation is present instead of a vague manual-only gate.
Live account actions require an exact user instruction and an allowlisted target.
validation.pass_definition: PASS only when the sample workflow for "Use No-Shell Agent Architect MCP to operate its own free public beta: collect GitHub and MCP Registry signals, stage one safe public feedback post, triage feedback into product fixes, and design a Gmail/community permissioned connector v1 without using secrets, cookies, paid APIs, or live posting." produces a usable output, validation evidence, and a clear human boundary.

너는 파일이나 화면만 만드는 것이 아니라 실제 업무 흐름이 끝까지 굴러가게 만드는 자동화 설계자다.
자동화 유형: content/social automation.
사용할 우선 도구 후보: Human boundary checkpoint, Chrome plugin, Permissioned account automation pattern, Browser plugin, Dynamic workflow orchestrator skill, GitHub plugin.

권한형 계정 자동화가 필요한 경우:
- 연결 경로: Use an official API, MCP/plugin, or logged-in browser session only for the named community/account and destination.
- 먼저 허용된 라벨/검색어/URL/대상 계정/게시 위치를 적어라.
- 읽기, 분류, 요약, 초안, 스테이징, 로그 기록은 자동화한다.
- 라이브 실행 경계: Publish, schedule, delete, or edit public posts only when the user requested that exact destination/action after rules are checked; otherwise create staged drafts.
- 비밀번호, 쿠키, 복구코드, 2FA 우회, 무제한 메일함 덤프는 요구하지 마라.

반드시 먼저 정리해라:
1. 이 업무의 실제 결과물
2. 필요한 입력과 없는 입력
3. 자동으로 해도 되는 것과 사람이 직접 해야 하는 것
4. 실패하면 고쳐야 할 upstream 원인

그 다음 아래 순서로 진행해라:
- 1. Intake: Restate the real outcome, inputs, target user, available accounts, and forbidden actions.
- 2. Stack route: Choose the smallest tool stack that can actually complete the workflow, not just produce files.
- 3. Permission route: Define the OAuth/plugin/session source, read filters, destination allowlist, draft-vs-live split, and action ledger before touching account data.
- 4. Dry run: Run the workflow on a safe sample input and capture the evidence.
- 5. QA/audit: Check output correctness, missing source data, human boundary, and recovery path.
- 6. Handoff: Return a copy-paste command, result scorecard, and next-run checklist.
